item.title: Rescuing a Windows Dynamic Disk Over USB with WSL2 and USB/IP
item.description: I pulled a 1 TB NVMe out of an old Windows box, dropped it in a USB enclosure, plugged it in, and Windows showed nothing. No drive letter, no “initialize this disk” prompt, nothing in Explorer. Disk Management listed it as Invalid, and the enclosure’s booklet said to “bring the disk online”, which silently did nothing. The data was completely intact. Windows was refusing on policy grounds, not because anything was broken, and getting it back meant going around the Windows storage stack entirely and handing the raw USB device to a Linux kernel that doesn’t share Windows’ opinions.

item.title: Cloud-Init ISOs in Pure Go with go-proxmox
item.description: Proxmox’s built-in cloud-init support is fine for the basics: a user, an SSH key, an IP config. It falls apart the second you want your own user-data, vendor-data or a real network-config, because the GUI and the ci* options only expose a handful of fields, and the escape hatch (cicustom pointing at snippet files) means getting files onto the Proxmox host’s filesystem first. The usual alternative is building a nocloud ISO yourself with genisoimage or mkisofs, which means a system dependency on whatever machine runs your automation, a different package name on every OS, and a subprocess to babysit.

item.title: Waiting on Proxmox: UPIDs, Tasks and WaitFor in Go
item.description: If you start automating Proxmox VE through the API, the first thing that trips you up is that almost nothing you ask it to do is finished when the HTTP call returns. Start a VM, clone a template, download an ISO to storage, delete a disk… the response is a single string that looks like a typo and the actual work is happening in a worker process on the node. If your next call depends on that work being done you have to go find out when it’s done.
